question: What is the mass number of an atom having 13 protons and 14 neutrons?
solution:
The correct answer is __**27 u**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The mass number of an atom is the sum of its protons and neutrons. In this case, it has 13 protons and 14 neutrons.
 
• The sum of 13 protons and 14 neutrons gives a mass number of 27.
 
• Mass number is represented by the symbol 'A' and is a whole number.
 
• The unit used for mass number is atomic mass unit (u), though it is often just a whole number without units.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Proton:**

 
 
• A proton is a subatomic particle found in the nucleus of every atom.
 
• It has a positive electric charge of +1 elementary charge.
 
• The number of protons in an atom defines the element (e.g., 13 protons define an atom as aluminum).
 
 
 
• **Neutron:**
 
 
• A neutron is a subatomic particle, also found in the nucleus of an atom, with no electric charge.
 
• Neutrons contribute to the atomic mass and stability of the nucleus.
 
 
 
• **Atomic Number (Z):**
 
 
• The atomic number is the number of protons in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• It determines the chemical properties of an element and its place in the periodic table.
 
 
 
• **Isotopes:**
 
 
• Isotopes are variants of a particular chemical element which differ in neutron number, and consequently in nucleon number.
 
• All isotopes of a given element have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons in each atom.
